name: Alexei Taylor
home: the ground floor of a Midtown walk-up
life: “I still remember my landlady teaching me the loud pedal.” People around the market by Market Flats know Alexei by a small Sunday habit. Alexei often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I rent the ground floor. I asked for lessons in exchange for living with somebody else's piano.
appearance: Alexei has a small notch in the left eyebrow. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. In conversation Alexei steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Alexei is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Alexei asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To exchange room in the flat for lessons.
family: Anthony Bell is Alexei’s older cousin. Alexei makes the call. Anthony is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The rescue hut mural*, Anthony says, “I sell postcards from the wrong angle and people prefer them.”
connections: Lena Osborne (piano owner). The owner and the ground-floor tenant have to agree on lessons as well as rent.

reactions.situation: A neighbor demands that the piano be taken off the landing
reactions.response: Alexei asks how much clear passage is needed today before arranging another move.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Alexei offers the worker something dry first and leaves it to them whether to pursue the apology.
